items.title: Mississauga Requires a Permit for Backyard Fireworks Over the Civic Holiday Weekend
items.summary: With the Civic Holiday long weekend approaching, the City of Mississauga is reminding residents that setting off fireworks in their backyard requires a permit first. Anyone planning a display should apply before the holiday to celebrate legally.

items.title: Mississauga Man Faces Impaired Driving Charge After E-Bike Crash in Guelph
items.summary: Guelph police say a Mississauga man was charged with impaired driving after officers found him injured on Tuesday night, having fallen off an e-bike he was riding at the time.

items.title: Mississauga Food Bank Seeks City Help to Waive Fees for Expansion
items.summary: As food insecurity grows in the city, a Mississauga food bank is asking the municipality to waive its share of development charges tied to an expansion project.

items.title: Rising Domestic Violence Cases Push Peel Shelters Past Capacity
items.summary: Local leaders say Peel Region's provincially funded emergency shelters are stretched thin as intimate partner violence cases climb, with outdated funding rules making it harder to keep up. Mississauga's mayor and Peel Regional Council are now pressing the province for additional support.

items.title: Power, Water and Noise Concerns Drive Push to Pause AI Data Centres in Mississauga and Toronto
items.summary: A Mississauga councillor is calling for a pause on new AI data centres as Toronto council considers its own proposed facilities. Critics point to the heavy power and water use, as well as noise, that these centres tend to bring.

items.title: Five-Year-Old Hospitalized After Being Pulled From Mississauga Backyard Pool
items.summary: A five-year-old was rushed to hospital late Tuesday morning after being pulled from a backyard pool in Mississauga, CP24 reports.

items.title: Child in Critical Condition After Being Rescued From Mississauga Home Pool
items.summary: Peel paramedics say a patient was rushed to hospital in critical condition after police responded to a reported drowning at a Mississauga home on Tuesday morning.

items.title: Free Walking Tours Highlight the Hidden History of Streetsville, Mississauga's Oldest Village
items.summary: Streetsville is often known for its restaurants, festivals and lively main street, but the neighborhood also holds more than 200 years of history, preserved better there than almost anywhere else in Mississauga. Free walking tours now offer a closer look at that heritage.

items.title: Century-Old Mississauga Coffee and Tea Maker Opens New Facility to Meet Cold Coffee Demand
items.summary: A coffee and tea manufacturer headquartered in Mississauga, founded more than 114 years ago, has opened a new facility as part of an effort to keep up with growing demand for cold coffee products.

items.title: Motion Could Prompt Mississauga to Review Cooling Protections for Apartment Tenants
items.summary: A motion before Mississauga council would direct city staff to review the current temperature bylaw and report back on possible cooling protections for apartment tenants, if it passes.
